history: From Jerry Thomas’s 1876 Bar-Tender’s Guide. "Improved" meant the addition of maraschino and absinthe to the basic spirit-sugar-bitters formula.
whyItWorks: Genever is malt-wine based, so it takes an Old Fashioned build the way rye does—the maraschino and absinthe sit on top of grain, not juniper.
steps: Rinse a chilled old fashioned glass with absinthe and discard the excess.
Stir genever, maraschino, syrup and bitters with ice until well chilled.
Strain over a large cube into the rinsed glass.
Express a lemon twist over the surface.
techniqueNotes: Oude genever, not jonge—the young style is closer to vodka and gives you nothing to work with.
The absinthe is a rinse, not an ingredient. Pour it out.

substitutions.notes: Rye is the closer match in weight; gin turns it into a Martinez cousin.
No true substitute for the rinse—omit rather than fake it.

name: Improved Holland Gin Cocktail
description: Jerry Thomas’s template applied to genever—malty, faintly funky, and closer to whiskey than to gin.
